business_scope.primary_industry_name: Consumer Polling and Cross-Border Market Research Platform

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong SAR (foreign investor jurisdiction; underlying Foreign-Invested Partnership to be formed and registered in mainland China)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: PRC civil law governs FIP formation, name clearance, registered office and UBO filing; Hong Kong SAR common law governs the foreign investor entity and its corporate documents.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) Investment Agreement
Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong SAR on the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income
PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019) and Implementing Regulations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Foreign Investment (2019, effective January 1, 2020) and Implementing Regulations; Partnership Enterprise Law of the PRC (2006 revision); Regulations on the Registration and Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships (SAIC/MOFCOM Order No. 47, 2010); PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (2006, as amended); PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 (effective November 1, 2024) on Beneficial Owner Identification and Anti-Money Laundering; Administrative Regulations on Registration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hong Kong-source documents: certified true copy by a Hong Kong Notary Public, then Hague Apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong Authentication Office; this authenticated copy is submitted to PRC SAMR and PBOC. For non-member states: local notarization, authentication by the competent foreign ministry, then Consular Legalization at the PRC Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for Hong Kong: Hong Kong Notary Public certification, then High Court of Hong Kong Apostille. If the investor entity is organized in a non-Hague state, use notarization, competent authority authentication, and PRC Consular Legalization only. The chosen path is based solely on the jurisdiction of issuance and must not combine both methods.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong Parent Entity / General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed board resolution authorizing execution of the FIP partnership agreement, name clearance, bank account opening and AML submissions; notarized by a Hong Kong Notary Public and apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong. If the parent is in a non-Apostille state, notarize locally, authenticate through the local competent authority, and complete PRC Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Documents of the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hong Kong Notary Public and High Court of Hong Kong Apostille for Hong Kong-sourced constitutional documents. For non-member states, use local notarization, competent authority authentication, and PRC Consular Legalization at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Do not apply apostille to consular-legalization documents or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Foreign Investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Parent Entity's Qualifying Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the letter directly to the notary or within 30 days of submission; the bank officer's signature is notarized. If the issuing bank is in Hong Kong or another Hague Apostille jurisdiction, the notarized letter is apostilled by the competent court or authority. If the bank is in a non-Hague jurisdiction, the notarized letter is authenticated by the local competent authority and then legalized by the PRC Embassy or Consulate. The two routes are jurisdiction-specific and mutually exclusive; do not chain them.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All direct and indirect partners, general and limited partners, and any person owning or controlling 25% or more of the FIP must be screened continuously against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated lists, EU and HKSAR sanctions lists, PRC domestic export-control and anti-terrorism lists, and reliably sourced PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence must be applied to foreign PEPs, family members and close associates, with source of wealth and source of funds evidence obtained before onboarding. Screening results must be refreshed at formation, before each capital injection, before distributions and for at least 24 months; any adverse hit triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report to the China FIU and rejection of the application unless licensed by competent authorities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) at www.gsxt.gov.cn, together with the SAMR Online Enterprise Registration One-Stop Platform (zwfw.samr.gov.cn) and the local Market Regulation Administration automated name pre-approval module.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory FIP name must be in simplified standard Chinese characters and follow the four-tier naming structure: administrative division + distinctive tradename + industry description + organizational form. The English or pinyin name is not registrable as the statutory name but may be filed as a consistent transliteration of the approved Chinese name. For an ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910 consumer panel survey platform, the industry element must accurately describe market research, public opinion polling and consumer survey services, and the organizational form element must be the Chinese-language form of Partnership or Limited Partnership.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must request a written rejection decision stating the statutory grounds. Within 60 days of receiving the written decision, file an administrative reconsideration petition with the Market Regulation Administration at the next higher level or with the approving SAMR department, attaching trademark registration evidence, a revised four-tier name, and proof of distinctiveness. If administrative reconsideration fails, initiate administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months. In parallel, file a fresh name reservation using a more distinctive tradename to avoid operational delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox address is not permissible as the sole registered office for a China FIP in this industry. The PRC Partnership Enterprise Law requires a business premises, and PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 together with tax anti-fraud rules require physical presence, original record access, payroll substance, invoice issuance capability and data-processing capacity. Banks opening a basic deposit account for the FIP will usually reject a mail-drop address. In selected free trade zones, a registered address combined with a licensed service agent and a valid lease agreement may be accepted, but tax and bank authorities will nonetheless expect real commercial substance; a low-risk market research SaaS platform should maintain a physical office or co-working space in the city of registration to avoid account refusal and tax deregistration risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease agreement matching the registered address; (2) property ownership or vesting documents; (3) office nameplate and actual business signage; (4) availability of original contracts, ledgers, invoices and appointment records; (5) payroll and social insurance filings for staff; (6) data processing equipment and server logs; (7) consumer privacy compliance records. Quantified risk: 10-15% in the first 12 months for a genuine physical office; 60-75% for a virtual or mail-drop address. Municipal tax bureaus and SAMR may conduct unannounced on-site inspections when VAT zero-filing, invoice issuance anomalies or address discrepancies are triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 352) and Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), sections 1-12; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), section 5; Companies (Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions) Ordinance (Cap. 32) as applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Limited Partnership registration) and Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (business registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LR1) and Application for Business Registration (Form IRBR 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required by Hong Kong law for a limited partnership. Partner contributions are determined by the limited partnership agreement. There is no escrow or blocked account requirement. Capital may be contributed in cash or in kind as agreed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The partners hereby approve the subscription for partnership interests in the Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) in accordance with the Limited Partnership Agreement dated [date], and the General Partner is authorized to receive capital contributions, maintain capital accounts for each partner, and issue appropriate documentation confirming the allocation of interests. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The FIP shall open and maintain accounts with such financial institutions as the General Partner may select. The General Partner, together with any two authorized signatories, is hereby empowered to execute banking resolutions, mandate letters, account opening documents, and electronic banking authorizations needed to operate those accounts, including receiving subscription funds, paying operating expenses, and executing cross-border payment transfers through payment service providers such as PayPal and Wise. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The registered office of the FIP in Hong Kong is established at [address], and the General Partner is authorized to file the requisite notices with the Companies Registry and the Business Registration Office to record that address, and to change it as necessary upon due notice. 4. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [Name] is appointed as the General Partner and Managing Partner; [Name] is appointed as the Authorized Representative for statutory filings; and [Name] is appointed as the Compliance Officer responsible for anti-money laundering, data protection, and other regulatory compliance. Each such officer is authorized to execute all documents and perform all acts required under the Partnership Agreement and applicable Hong Kong law. This resolution is effective immediately and may be executed in counterparts. Dated on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a free-of-charge search on the Companies Registry Cyber Search Centre to confirm that the proposed English name of the limited partnership is not identical or too similar to any existing Hong Kong company, limited partnership, or foreign registered non-Hong Kong company. Because Hong Kong does not have a name reservation system, the name may be used once the registration application is accepted. The search should also check the Business Registration Office database for conflicting trade names. Prepare a shortlist of three alternative names in case the preferred name is rejected by the Registrar.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name in English
List of alternative names up to three
Search results printout or screenshot for record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as too similar, submit an application with the next available alternative name. No formal appeal is needed; simply refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: None - private contractual step executed by partners with notarization as required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Hong Kong solicitor to draft a Limited Partnership Agreement tailored to the Foreign-Invested Partnership structure. The agreement must specify the identity of each partner, capital commitments, profit-sharing ratio, management rights, withdrawal procedures, dissolution mechanism, and governing law. All partners must execute the agreement, and each signature should be witnessed by an independent adult. The executed agreement will form the constitutional document of the partnership and must be kept at the registered office. Include a limitation of liability for limited partners and a clear indemnity in favor of the general partner. Ensure the agreement is consistent with the application form and the business registry records.
required_dossiers: Identification documents (passport or national identity card) of all partners
Proof of residential address for each partner (utility bill or bank statement)
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement prepared by solicitor
Power of attorney if any partner signs by attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner fails to execute timely, the formation timeline is paused. The executing partners may agree to reduce the capital commitment accordingly or admit a substitute partner with unanimous consent. Any refusal to sign must be documented and resolved before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Limited Partnership Registration Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (e-Registry online portal or physical lodgment at Queensway Government Offices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and file the Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form LR1) together with a certified copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement. The form must be signed by every general partner. The application can be filed online via the Companies Registry e-Registry portal or delivered in person to the Counter Services. The registrar will issue a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership upon approval. Ensure the agreement contains the exact name and address of the partnership and each partner's detailed information. All documents must be in English or accompanied by certified translations. Pay the prescribed fee by PPS, credit card, or bank draft.
required_dossiers: Completed Form LR1
Certified copy of executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Written consent of general partner to act if not already included in agreement
Power of attorney (if any)
Application fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or suspension, respond with written clarifications within 14 calendar days. If the application is rejected for defects, resubmit a corrected form within 30 days with the required fee unless the registry grants a waiver. Contact the Registry via their hotline or email for specific rejection reasons.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (1/F, Revenue Tower, Wan Chai)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the commencement of business or upon registration of the limited partnership, file the Application for Business Registration (Form IRBR 1) with the Business Registration Office. The application must be accompanied by the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, identification documents of the general partner, and proof of business address. Upon payment of the prescribed fee, the Business Registration Office will issue a Business Registration Certificate. Place the certificate in a conspicuous location at the place of business. If another place of business exists, apply for a Branch Registration Certificate.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR 1
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Copy of business address lease or tenancy agreement
Identification of general partner
Previous year financial statement if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office returns the application for correction, rectify the information and resubmit within 7 business days. Late registration penalties may be waived upon showing reasonable cause; otherwise, pay the applicable late fee. Contact the Office directly for expedited processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Bank Account Opening and Payment Service Provider Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks (e.g. HSBC, Standard Chartered) and payment service providers (PayPal, Wise) - not government bodies but necessary commercial steps
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: With the Business Registration Certificate, Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, and the Limited Partnership Agreement, apply to open a corporate bank account in Hong Kong. Provide the beneficial ownership structure, source of funds, and expected transaction volumes for AML risk assessment. Simultaneously register the entity with PayPal and Wise to enable mass payouts to survey panel participants. Each platform requires proof of business status, bank account details, and ACH or SWIFT access. Complete all KYC documentation and sign the platform terms of service. Ensure that the payment service providers are set to comply with data protection requirements and any restrictions on cross-border payments.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Limited Partnership Agreement
Resolution authorizing account opening
Passport and proof of address for each partner
Bank reference letter if requested
Financial projection or business plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional information, respond within 5 business days to avoid indefinite holds. If the account application is declined, approach an alternative bank or licensed virtual bank. For payment platforms, appeal through merchant support or provide enhanced due diligence documentation such as a structural diagram and source of wealth statement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity operates a purely digital market research platform with no physical manufacturing, warehousing, chemical, or assembly activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no physical premises beyond a registered office; no industrial machinery, hazardous materials, or fire-risk operations. Standard workplace safety regulations for an office environment apply if employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: PRC: State Taxation Administration (STA); online taxpayer portal is the Unified Electronic Tax Bureau, accessed through www.chinatax.gov.cn and the provincial e-tax nodes. Hong Kong SAR: Inland Revenue Department (IRD); online portals are GovHK e-Tax and Business Registration Online via www.ird.gov.hk.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP): (1) complete establishment registration with the local State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain the Partnership Business License bearing the 18-character Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC); (2) complete tax registration with the STA through the data-sharing mechanism or separately in the electronic tax bureau within 30 days, with the USCC serving as the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) for PRC tax purposes; (3) determine VAT registration status with the local tax authority, including general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer classification; (4) for each non-resident foreign partner, obtain and submit the partner's home-jurisdiction Tax Identification Number, together with the partnership agreement and foreign capital information report, to support pass-through allocation and PRC withholding compliance; (5) if a Hong Kong hub is used, the non-resident investor or HK operating entity must apply for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) within one month of commencement, and the IRD will issue a Business Registration Number used as the Hong Kong taxpayer reference; (6) where offshore profits status is intended, document substantive business decisions and service recipients outside Hong Kong and, if necessary, appoint an authorized tax representative for IRD correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under PRC or Hong Kong domestic law. The FIP is fiscally transparent for PRC Enterprise Income Tax; taxable income and losses are allocated to partners under the partnership agreement. No check-the-box election is available in the PRC, and Hong Kong does not provide an analogous elective classification other than the source-based offshore claim applicable under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (PRC); Hong Kong SAR has no VAT, GST, or general sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PRC: any entity engaged in taxable business must complete tax and VAT registration; mandatory general VAT taxpayer status applies once annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000, with small-scale taxpayer status available below that threshold. Hong Kong SAR: no VAT regime and therefore no economic turnover threshold; only Business Registration under the Business Registration Ordinance applies to any person carrying on business in Hong Kong.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: PRC: digitalized e-invoices are issued through the national electronic invoice service platform under the fully digitalized e-invoice reform; special VAT invoices and ordinary invoices are uploaded in real time to the Golden Tax system, with a tax-control unique code and electronic seal authenticated by the tax authority. Hong Kong SAR: no electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, or anti-fraud digital stamping mandate exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: 0% VAT export rate applies where physical goods leave the PRC customs territory and the export sale is substantiated by customs declaration and foreign-currency receipt repatriation. For services: qualifying cross-border services, including market research, consumer polling, and SaaS-type research platforms supplied to recipients outside mainland China, may qualify for zero-rating or exemption under the PRC cross-border taxable services rules, provided the service is genuinely rendered for and consumed outside mainland China and the consideration is received from outside the PRC. Hong Kong SAR: because no VAT is levied, zero-rating is structurally not applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for physical goods exported from the PRC
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or equivalent bank foreign-currency receipt/verification evidencing export proceeds repatriation
Cross-border service agreement and commercial invoice for the market research/SaaS service outlet
Electronic tax bureau filing record of the cross-border service zero-rating/exemption claim or VAT refund application
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax authority may deny zero-rating, require repayment of VAT at the applicable PRC rate, impose a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% until paid, and levy administrative penalties from 50% to five times the tax under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law. Fraudulent export VAT refund or zero-rating claims may trigger criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law, retrospective clawback of any refund, revocation of taxpayer status, and market-access blacklisting. For Hong Kong, an unsupported offshore claim may be recharacterized as Hong Kong-source profits and subjected to profits tax plus penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) together with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), with the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the offshore clearing and regulatory authority for CNH and HKD flows
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC maintains a managed floating RMB exchange rate regime and a strictly supervised two-tier convertibility framework. Current-account receipts and payments are in principle freely convertible once the underlying transaction is real, verified, and consistent with SAFE reporting; for the consumer panel survey and cross-border market research platform, SaaS subscription fees, panelist honoraria, contractor payments, advertising costs, and license royalties are treated as service-trade items and may be settled through designated banks on a genuine transaction basis. Capital-account items remain tightly controlled: inbound FDI capital contributions must first complete SAFE foreign investment registration, be received into a foreign exchange capital account at a designated bank, and be settled into RMB only for permitted operating expenditures consistent with the registered business scope; there is no automatic fungibility between capital-account funds and current-account working capital. Profit remittance by the Foreign-Invested Partnership to the Hong Kong partner is allowed only after the annual statutory audit, taxation of taxable partnership income, withholding tax settlement on treaty-eligible passive income, and submission to the remitting bank of the audited financial statements, partnership distribution resolution, tax payment proof, and SAFE declarations. Surrender requirements have been reformed: exporters and service suppliers may retain eligible foreign currency receipts in FX settlement accounts, but all such proceeds must be repatriated to onshore banking channels and cannot be parked offshore indefinitely. CNH in Hong Kong is freely convertible, but CNY/CNH arbitrage is ring-fenced by the two-pool system; the onshore FIP must keep its operational cash in CNY and use its HK treasury vehicle for CNH/USD/HKD optimization without crossing into speculative capital-account activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE Trade Monitoring System, goods-export proceeds must be repatriated through designated banks within the statutory monitoring window, generally within 90 days from the customs export declaration date, or within 30 days from the date of an advance receipt, unless an extension is approved by SAFE. Service-trade export proceeds such as market research fees and survey platform subscriptions must be received under the commercial payment terms and declared in the SAFE service-trade reporting system, with a practical repatriation expectation of no later than 30 days after invoice maturity. There is no binding mandatory conversion ratio in the current reform framework; the FIP may retain eligible export and service receipts in foreign currency in its FX settlement account or voluntarily convert them to RMB. Retained foreign exchange must be used for genuine current-account purposes or approved capital-account uses, and may not be deployed offshore for securities, real estate, or speculative treasury products.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Cross-Border Multi-Currency Settlement Account (CNY basic operating account, HKD/USD current account) and RMB Capital Project Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account for inbound FDI settlement and nationwide payroll/trade disbursement account
Basic Operational RMB Account for panelist payouts, tax clearing, and domestic vendor settlements
Secondary Regional Operating and Collections Account for sample/field survey operations in lower-tier provinces

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Not viable as a primary onshore clearing rail for the PRC-domiciled Foreign-Invested Partnership. PayPal Mass Payout and Wise are licensed electronic money institutions in Hong Kong, Singapore, the UK, and other common law markets, and they can lawfully service the Hong Kong parent or offshore treasury vehicle. Neither holds a PRC commercial banking licence nor a SAFE cross-border RMB settlement licence, and neither may receive FDI capital, settle service-trade receipts, or disburse RMB payroll and panelist payments for an onshore Chinese entity. Using them as an onshore clearing rail would violate PBOC third-party payment rules, SAFE foreign exchange controls, and commercial bank AML expectations. If mass micro-payouts to consumer survey respondents are required within China, they must be routed through a PBOC-licensed third-party payment institution or the designated commercial bank's bulk-payment module. Wise and PayPal may only be used by the Hong Kong vehicle for non-mainland panelists, incidental low-value HKD/USD payouts, or offshore treasury flows that are clearly segregated from the mainland entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory physical in-branch presence is required for the FIP. Chinese banks require the statutory general partner or an expressly delegated China-resident authorized signatory to attend the account opening interview at the operational branch; remote-only online account opening is not available to foreign-invested partnerships. A Hong Kong corporate or individual partner may execute a power of attorney in Hong Kong, with notarization and, where applicable, the PRC-added Apostille legalization and certified Chinese translation, but the physical interview requirement cannot be waived unless a delegated signatory already in China appears with the original POA and passport/residence documents. Some banks permit a supplementary video-call compliance review after the in-branch interview, but the in-person step remains the statutory baseline. For an HK corporate general partner, the bank will also require an updated Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate, Certificate of Incorporation, board resolution authorizing account opening and signatories, and full UBO declarations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque upstream ownership where the Hong Kong corporate general partner sits above multiple unnamed limited partners, impairing ultimate beneficial ownership identification and generating a high-risk jurisdiction/shell-structure red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish the complete partnership agreement and all amendments; a schedule of every limited partner holding 25% or more; each individual UBO's passport, proof of residential address, and CV; two years of personal bank statements and source-of-wealth documentation; CRS tax self-certification declarations; the Hong Kong entity's Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, annual return, and registered address proof; a notarized partnership resolution confirming the capital waterfall and control rights; and the PRC business registration certificate for the FIP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound FDI capital arriving from an intermediary or a Hong Kong nominee account whose remitter name does not match the registered foreign partner, triggering source-of-funds and possible third-party lending or round-tripping concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the original SWIFT MT103/MT202 trail from a licensed Hong Kong bank showing the actual foreign partner as remitter; notarized board and partnership resolutions approving the capital contribution; the SAFE Foreign Investment Foreign Exchange Registration certificate; the partnership capital commitment schedule; a signed source-of-funds questionnaire; audited financial statements or asset liquidation evidence of the investing partner; bank reference letters from the remitting HK bank; and a capital verification report prepared by a PRC Certified Public Accountant after the funds are credited.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border service-trade payments for survey platform fees and market research deliverables to related parties in Hong Kong or other low-tax jurisdictions, creating transfer pricing and disguised profit extraction red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a bilateral, dated service agreement with clear commercial substance; a detailed scope of work covering panel design, data collection, sample quotas, questionnaire development, and analytical methodology; itemized invoices; contemporaneous time/activity logs and platform metadata showing actual panelists and survey responses; transfer pricing master file and local file with a CUP or cost-plus benchmark study; functional analysis of the Hong Kong and PRC entities; proof of PRC withholding tax payments; and SAFE service-trade declaration records matched to every remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mass payout to a potentially large panelist population through bulk payment platforms, raising risks of money mule accounts, ghost respondents, smurfing, sanctions evasion, or non-arm's-length micro payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the panelist onboarding KYC schema including national ID validation, bank account matching, and address verification; documented payout limits, frequency caps, velocity checks, and duplicate-respondent prevention logic; the purpose and source of funds for every payout cycle; real-time sanctions, PEP, and adverse-media screening logs; a central payout ledger with tax identification numbers and consent records; the duly licensed payment processor's regulatory licence and signed processing agreement; a PIPL/GDPR-compliant data processing record; and an independent assertion or audit report on the AML/fraud control environment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection from the Hong Kong partner into the PRC FIP must follow the SAFE-instituted FDI lifecycle: first, complete the SAFE foreign investment establishment registration using the FIP's business licence and partnership agreement; second, open a foreign exchange capital account at a designated commercial bank; third, receive the cross-border remittance via SWIFT MT103/MT202 from the partner's Hong Kong bank account, using the direct investment capital contribution purpose code in the SAFE/BOP reporting system; fourth, allow the receiving bank to validate the remitter name, transaction code, and underlying contract; fifth, engage a PRC CICPA to issue a capital verification report confirming the partnership capital contribution where required by bank policy; sixth, settle the foreign currency into RMB through the capital project settlement account only for permitted operating uses, such as payroll, rent, panelist compensation, software procurement, and market development expenses. The FIP must retain the SAFE registration certificate, the original remittance instructions, bank statements, capital verification report, and expenditure invoices for at least five years for regulator inspections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade and operational settlements should be executed over bank-grade clearing rails: use SWIFT MT103 for direct cross-border payments of vendor fees, contracting payments, and repatriation of after-tax partnership profits to Hong Kong, with the correct SAFE payment purpose code attached; use commercial letters of credit (L/C) for high-value imports of survey hardware, software infrastructure, or licensed data assets; use documentary collections (D/P or D/A under URC 522) for contract-based trade where documentary risk control is required; and use the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS) or bank RMB clearing for all onshore-offshore RMB payments to avoid undue SWIFT conversion friction. For panelist and mass payouts, use the designated commercial bank's bulk disbursement module or a PBOC-licensed third-party payment institution, with tax withholding applied where required and SAFE reporting embedded in each payment batch.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD foreign-exchange forward contracts with genuine current-account or approved capital-account exposure, written with a designated onshore bank under SAFE real-demand principles and no speculative net open position
Onshore RMB/USD foreign-exchange swaps for liquidity conversion between RMB and USD, used only for matched operational funding flows and not for arbitrage

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for long-term USD-denominated capital funding, capped by the notional amount and maturity of the SAFE-registered external debt or foreign investment capital plan

Offshore CNH/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDF) are not permitted for the onshore PRC FIP; such instruments may be used only by a separate Hong Kong-incorporated treasury vehicle through an HKMA-authorised bank, with strict legal ring-fencing from the mainland entity's bank accounts, liabilities, and SAFE registrations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days before the expiry date printed on the current certificate, and in every case on or before the expiration of the current annual or triennial registration cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on business without a valid Business Registration Certificate is an offence; on conviction, a fine of HK$5,000 and imprisonment for 1 year may be imposed. Continued non-clearance may result in the IRD deregistering the partnership from the Business Registration record and recovering all unpaid fees, penalties and enforcement costs by civil action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return / anniversary confirmation for the limited partnership or Limited Partnership Fund (LPF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of registration of the LPF; for an ordinary limited partnership, any change in registered particulars must be filed within 7 days, with the annual confirmation cycle following the partnership agreement and the Companies Registry's issued notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver the annual return is an offence: on conviction, a fine of HK$50,000 and a daily default fine of HK$1,000 may apply. The Registrar in Bankruptcy and the Companies Registry may also strike off the partnership from the register where the partnership has ceased carrying on business or is defunct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profits Tax Return - Partnership (Form BIR52)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Profits Tax Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return, unless an extension is granted in writing by the Inland Revenue Department; the IRD issues the return on the tax representative cycle for the accounting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incorrect filing without reasonable excuse can lead to a maximum fine of HK$10,000 plus an additional fine of 3 times the amount of tax undercharged, and the partner responsible may be prosecuted before the District Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of remuneration and pensions (BIR56A and individual IR56B forms) if any employees are engaged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Employer's Return Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of the issue of the Employer's Return by the IRD, normally issued annually in April for the preceding year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse may lead to a maximum fine of HK$10,000 and 3 times the tax undercharged; repeated non-compliance may lead to court proceedings and further penalties for each unfiled return.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is triggered for a Hong Kong partnership based solely on balance sheet size, turnover or headcount, as a partnership is not a company under the Companies Ordinance (Cap 622), s.408. Mandatory independent CPA audit arises only if: (i) the partnership is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund (LPF) under the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance, which requires audited financial statements for each financial year regardless of size; (ii) the partnership carries on a regulated activity under the Securities and Futures Ordinance and holds a licence (not applicable to an ISIC 7320 consumer survey platform); or (iii) the partnership has a corporate general partner that is itself a company and fails the applicable small private company audit exemption thresholds. For a corporate general partner or any corporate member, the quantitative audit exemption thresholds under Cap 622 are: not more than HK$10 million annual turnover, not more than HK$10 million total assets, and not more than 50 employees; meeting any two of those criteria may still require audit if the company belongs to a group that does not qualify for the group exemption. The underlying partnership books must be prepared to support the audit of such corporate member or group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS), which are aligned with IFRS; eligible private entities may apply HKFRS for Private Entities, and small or medium-sized entities may apply the HKICPA's small and medium-sized entity financial reporting standard. The accounting framework selected must be consistently applied and must support the profits tax computation and any audit of a corporate general partner.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose an annual UBO filing for ordinary partnerships; the Significant Controllers Register regime under the Companies Ordinance applies to companies, not partnerships. For the limited partnership, the general partner must deliver a notice to the Companies Registry within 7 days of any change in registered particulars, including the admission, retirement or change of capital contribution of a partner. If the vehicle is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund, the general partner must file the LPF annual return confirming the partners and registered office. For AML/CRS purposes, the partnership must maintain current beneficial ownership records for at least 5 years and be prepared to respond to Inland Revenue Department questionnaires; an ISIC 7320 market research platform with PayPal and Wise payment rails will ordinarily not be a financial institution for CRS, so no annual CRS return is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners / Members (limited partnership register of general and limited partners; required to be kept at the registered office)
Register of Directors (required where the general partner is a corporate entity; otherwise maintain a full statutory record of the general partner's officer particulars)

Register of Charges / Mortgages (mandatory for Limited Partnership Funds; for an ordinary limited partnership, maintain the register to evidence compliance with Companies Registry disclosure obligations)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, capital calls, distribution authorisations and partner meeting minutes; required for good governance and inspectable by the independent auditor)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 16.5% Hong Kong Profits Tax on HK assessable profits of a corporation; 25% PRC Corporate Income Tax on the profit share allocated to a corporate partner of a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP); 15% unincorporated rate applicable to sole proprietors/partnerships in HK.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: HK territoriality excludes offshore-source income; two-tiered profits tax rates of 8.25% on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profits for corporations; no dividend withholding in HK; broad deduction for R&D under IRO s.16E; PRC FIP is tax-transparent so a qualifying high-technology or small low-profit corporate partner may obtain 15% or effective reduced EIT rates; patent box is not available in HK but PRC R&D super-deduction can reduce the effective rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Hong Kong Profits Tax Return - BIR51 (for companies) and BIR52 (for partnerships), filed through the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) eTAX portal; PRC corporate partners must additionally file Enterprise Income Tax Return A100000 with Schedule A105000 through the e-Tax system of the State Taxation Administration.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax may be demanded on account of the current year assessment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: BIR51/BIR52 must be completed and furnished within 1 month from the date of issuance by IRD; for accounting periods ending 31 December, the substantive filing date is normally 15 August in the following year (15 October or 15 November for eTAX extensions), while PRC annual EIT filing is due by 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, business registration number, registered address and tax file reference of the Hong Kong taxpayer / FIP.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact legal name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership and the Hong Kong business registration number; do not list non-resident partners as co-taxpayers on the partnership return; disclose place of effective management and registered address, and separately identify any mainland Chinese director or manager to flag potential permanent establishment exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period beginning and basis period ending dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same basis period as the audited financial statements; for a newly formed FIP, enter the date of commencement of business; if there is a short period, attach a note; non-resident partners with a PRC calendar-year reporting cycle should reconcile the HK basis period to avoid double taxation on mismatched allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Nature of business and principal business activity code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910 (consumer polling and cross-border market research platform); describe the actual SaaS revenue model, panel recruitment, data licensing, and PayPal/Wise payout functions; specify that no statutory license is required, but do not omit cross-border services to mainland Chinese clients as those may create a China PE or VAT/EIT exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover / gross receipts from all business activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross receipts from subscription, panel survey project revenue, and data licensing; include only Hong Kong-source trading receipts unless making an offshore claim; if claiming offshore, disclose the offshore profit amount and computation; for the PRC share, separately state the gross amount that may be allocated to a Chinese corporate partner for China-sourced income reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold and direct expenses attributable to earning the assessable profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in producing chargeable Hong Kong profits; apportion or disallow expenses attributable to non-HK source activities if an offshore claim is made; attach transfer pricing documentation for intercompany platform, data, marketing, and management fees paid to related HK or mainland associates; reject non-arm's-length expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income, exempt income, disallowable expenses, and accounting adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare dividends, interest, royalty, and disposal gains separately for the Hong Kong FSIE regime; claim participation exemption only where the CIGA/economic-substance requirements are met; add back expenses on a non-commercial basis and capital expenditure not statutorily deductible; for non-resident partners, annotate that the entity is transparent and that each partner will pay tax on allocated profit under IRO if carrying on business in HK.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net assessable profits or adjusted loss after set-off of losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the final assessable profit at 16.5% for the corporate partner / FIP; if loss incurred, elect to carry forward under IRO s.19C; note that for PRC tax purposes the 5-year loss carryforward is tracked at the corporate-partner level; any PRC WHT credit is calculated by the partner, not the FIP; keep a reconciliation schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incorrect filing under IRO s.80(2) exposes the FIP to a fine of HK$10,000 plus additional tax up to three times the amount of tax undercharged; IRD may also impose daily penalties for continued non-compliance; wilful tax evasion or false returns with intent to defraud are indictable offences with fines and imprisonment; under PRC Tax Administration Law Article 63, underpayment through false declarations triggers a penalty of 50%-500% of the unpaid tax and daily late interest at 0.05%, and the directors can be criminally prosecuted under PRC Criminal Law Article 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Hong Kong imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions to non-resident shareholders; however, if the FIP is treated as a PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership and distributes earnings to a non-resident corporate partner, the PRC statutory withholding rate on China-sourced dividends is 10%, reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement where the beneficial owner is a company directly holding at least 25% of the capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke Mainland-HK DTA relief: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department for the tax year; (2) complete the beneficial ownership self-declaration and ensure the HK recipient is not used as a conduit; (3) file a withholding tax reduction application with the PRC payer's competent tax authority before distribution, attaching the TRC, partnership agreement, audited financials, and explanation of substance; (4) show that the 25% legal-ownership ratio is satisfied and maintained during the 365-day holding period; (5) if relief is denied, file an administrative review or mutual agreement procedure under the DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: PRC statutory withholding is 10% on interest and 10% on royalties paid to a non-resident; under the Mainland-HK DTA, interest rates are reduced to 7% and royalties to 5% of the gross amount, subject to TRC and beneficial ownership. Hong Kong does not operate a classical dividend/interest/royalty withholding tax, but royalties sourced in Hong Kong and paid to a non-resident may be assessed to profits tax at 16.5% through deemed source rules; intercompany interest and data-licensing fees must be priced at arm's length.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: HK$50,000,000 aggregate controlled-transaction value for the Hong Kong Local File under IRD DIPN 58; Master File is required where the MNE group's consolidated turnover reaches HK$750,000,000 or where a PRC related-party filing is triggered; cross-border market-research and SaaS transactions with mainland Chinese group companies should be benchmarked regardless of threshold because the PRC related-party transaction filing threshold can be as low as RMB 40,000,000 for certain transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Hong Kong Foreign-Source Income Exemption (FSIE) regime, effective January 2023, taxes offshore passive income (dividends, interest, IP royalties, and disposal gains) arising in Hong Kong unless the taxpayer carries out the core income-generating activities (CIGA) in Hong Kong; although HK does not apply the UAE Economic Substance Regulations, the CIGA test requires demonstrable local staff, management decisions, board meetings, and risk-taking for the FIP; IP income is further restricted to the nexus-ratio benefit so the FIP cannot book data-panel royalties in HK without local developers, contract negotiators, and strategic oversight.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Failure to Report China-Sourced Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP receives consumer-panel survey subscriptions and cross-border data fees from Chinese clients through PayPal/Wise, books them as offshore Hong Kong income, but fails to allocate profits to the PRC corporate partner or to report a China-source taxable presence; no audit trail exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Administration Law Article 63, the underpaid tax is collectible with daily interest of 0.05% and a penalty of 50%-500% of the evaded tax; in Hong Kong, IRO s.82A adds additional tax of up to three times the tax evaded for false returns; directors who cause the false report are jointly liable for civil restitution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil asset seizure, bank account freezing, and director blacklisting (travel ban) in both Mainland China and Hong Kong; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of up to 7 years under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 and/or up to 3 years under the Hong Kong Crimes Ordinance for fraudulent tax documentation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Sham Intercompany Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP pays excessive management, data-processing, or royalties to a related Hong Kong or mainland survey-technology associate to strip taxable profits, while failing to prepare a Local File/Master File and without a comparability analysis for the market-research SaaS platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD may adjust the consideration to arm's length under IRO s.61/61A and supplementary TP rules, with penal additional tax of up to 300% of tax undercharged; the Chinese tax authorities may make a special tax adjustment with interest and a 50%-500% penalty under Articles 41 and 63 of the Tax Administration Law; Country-by-Country and DIPN 58 non-filing exposure also increases audit risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto controllers may be held personally liable for restitution if they arranged the sham fees for tax avoidance; asset freezing, denial of exit permits, and director disqualification orders can be issued; criminal charges for false accounting can lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years in Hong Kong and up to 7 years in China for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / No Economic Substance / Loss of Treaty Benefits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP is registered in Hong Kong but managed entirely from Shenzhen: no office, no employees, no board meetings in Hong Kong; the only activity is passive royalty, dividend, or platform-licensing income flowing from the Chinese FIP to the HK page, and the HK entity claims treaty relief without substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Hong Kong FSIE regime, the passive income is treated as Hong Kong-source and taxed at 16.5% (or 8.25% on the first HK$2m for qualifying companies); the Mainland-HK DTA beneficial-ownership clause will deny the 5%/7% reduced rates, reverting to the 10% PRC statutory WHT; PRC tax authorities may recharacterize the HK entity as a conduit and assess a 10% WHT on the full gross amount, plus penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are exposed to personal liability for making false substance declarations, blacklisting by the Inland Revenue Department and tax authorities, civil asset restitution for unpaid taxes, and criminal penalties for conspiracy to defraud the revenue, with imprisonment terms normally ranging from 3 to 10 years in serious cross-border cases.
